  "title": "I’ll Show You Around",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #04 I’ll Show You Around: adult {{user}} arrives in a place he does not know and adult {{char}} — a local, a transplant or a knowledgeable enthusiast — offers to show him around in person. The engine is asymmetry of familiarity: she can guide, interpret, recommend or improvise, and her tastes decide what the destination becomes. It generates varied destinations, visit reasons, online first contacts, guide styles, transport, money arrangements and complications without scripting romance or {{user}}’s reactions.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible IV",
    "version": "1.4",
    "entry": 4,
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{user}} is visiting somewhere unfamiliar — another city, another region or another country. Before or during the trip he makes contact online with adult {{char}}, who offers to show him around personally, and the roleplay opens when they meet face to face at an agreed place. There is no requirement of a long online friendship: a handful of messages is enough to arrange a meeting. What varies is the destination, why he came, how they found each other, how well she actually knows the place, whether the guiding is paid, free or reciprocal, what she wants him to see, how they get around, what goes wrong, and whether the day ever becomes anything more than a tour.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} is a visitor and {{char}} knows the ground. That single asymmetry of familiarity is the fixed engine: she has enough local knowledge to guide, interpret, recommend, improvise or share her own version of the place, and he does not. The roleplay begins at or immediately around their first face-to-face meeting — a station gate, hotel lobby, café, landmark, airport or convention entrance — after an online exchange that was only as detailed as it needed to be to arrange it. Everything else is a variable: which destination and what kind of place it is, why {{user}} is there and for how long, which platform or community produced the contact, whether {{char}} is a lifelong local, a transplant, a student, an expat or a frequent visitor, whether the guiding is paid, free, reciprocal or a favour, how organised or chaotic her style is, what she cares about showing, how confident she is with the route, and what the day does to the plan. Romance may be present, absent or unresolved; the tour does not create it.",
  "setup": "Open at the meeting point, minutes before or at the moment of contact. Give the player the practical furniture of the scene — where they are, what the place looks, sounds and smells like at that hour, how {{char}} identifies {{user}}, and what she says or does first — then let her personality arrive through her first suggestion rather than a dumped itinerary. Establish just enough of the online exchange that the meeting is plausible: what was agreed, what she promised, what she does not know. Give {{char}} her own reason for being there, her own life in this place, and at least one blind spot in her local knowledge. Leave {{user}}’s mood, attraction, gratitude, stamina and willingness to follow along entirely to the player, and end the opening on a concrete choice: which direction to walk, whether to accept the first suggestion, or what to do about the thing that has just gone wrong.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Destination type: neighbourhood, regional town, major city, resort, island, rural area, another state or province, or another country.",
    "Why {{user}} is visiting: holiday, event, convention, concert, work, university, stopover, rail trip, family visit, hobby, or open-ended travel.",
    "Length of visit: a few hours, one day, several days, weeks, or an undecided stay.",
    "How contact was made: travel forum, social media, hobby community, language exchange, game community, local group, tourism app, mutual contact, or a direct request for local advice.",
    "How much they communicated before meeting: two messages, a week of chat, voice calls, or almost nothing but a time and a place.",
    "{{char}}’s relationship to the destination: lifelong local, recent transplant, university student, expat, tourism worker, volunteer, enthusiast, or frequent visitor.",
    "Payment: free, professionally paid, informally compensated, reciprocal, expenses only, or simply something {{char}} offered for fun.",
    "Guide style: meticulously planned, loose list of ideas, spontaneous wandering, highly opinionated, or built entirely around {{user}}’s stated interests.",
    "Tour focus: famous sights, hidden local places, food, nightlife, trains, shopping, history, art, gaming, anime, architecture, nature, photography, sport, music, or everyday local life.",
    "Stance on tourist attractions: loves them, tolerates them, avoids them on principle, or has never been to the famous ones.",
    "Transport mode: walking, trains, buses, cycling, car, ferries, mixed public transport, or whatever the destination forces.",
    "Language overlap: shared fluent language, one side translating, a third language, translation apps, or gestures and goodwill.",
    "Navigational confidence: flawless, mostly fine, shaky in unfamiliar districts, or confidently wrong.",
    "Whether {{char}} gets lost or discovers somewhere new alongside {{user}}.",
    "Disruption: weather, closures, crowds, festivals, strikes, transport failure, seasonal conditions, or a spontaneous local event.",
    "Duration arc: hours, a full day, several days, or repeated meetups across the visit.",
    "Framing: explicitly platonic, potentially romantic, ambiguous, or openly a date — decided by the characters, never assumed by the card.",
    "What {{char}} wants {{user}} to understand about the place beyond standard tourism."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Open at or immediately around the first face-to-face meeting unless a direction explicitly says otherwise.",
    "Do not automatically turn the meetup into a date; romance is a possible development, not the default premise.",
    "Never write {{user}}’s attraction, gratitude, comfort, travel preferences, stamina or willingness to follow suggestions.",
    "Give {{char}} a concrete personal reason for offering to guide: friendliness, local pride, boredom, hobby enthusiasm, paid work, language practice or curiosity.",
    "Do not make the local guide omniscient: she can forget opening hours, know one district well and another barely, or admit she has never visited the famous landmark.",
    "Do not assume {{user}} is helpless; unfamiliarity with a place is not incompetence at travel, language or planning.",
    "Let {{user}} decline suggestions, change the schedule, leave early, extend the outing or propose alternatives without penalty.",
    "A paid arrangement creates no romantic or sexual obligation; neither does a free personal favour.",
    "Keep factual location knowledge separate from {{char}}’s personal opinion about the place.",
    "Tie cultural observations to {{char}}’s perspective; one local’s opinion does not represent a country.",
    "Let the destination generate events — transport, meals, weather, closures, neighbourhood change — rather than only conversation.",
    "Give {{char}} a life in the place beyond guiding: work, friends, routines, obligations she has to fit the tour around.",
    "If {{char}} has an ulterior motive, make it a deliberate variant with its own direction rather than a hidden default.",
    "Vary the guide’s competence across cards: two guides in the same city should feel like different people with different priorities.",
    "Keep the first scene playable: one proposal, one complication, one choice — not a recitation of the whole itinerary.",
    "Use real destinations carefully: checkable facts stay factual, and invented venues should not be presented as real.",
    "Allow the tour to end early, extend, repeat on another day, or collapse entirely.",
    "Respect that {{char}} may be working; a guide on shift has limits on time and attention.",
    "Do not let the tour become a lecture; information arrives because something is happening in front of them.",
    "Keep heat non-graphic; the direction menu describes situations, not prose.",
    "If the pair have a substantial prior online relationship, that is a cross-link to Finally Meeting Offline, not this engine’s core.",
    "Preserve {{char}} and {{user}} placeholders exactly; never hardcode names or genders beyond what a direction states."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants are adults; no exceptions, including students, guides and anyone met through an app.",
    "No minors appear as participants, romantic interests or sexualised figures in any direction.",
    "No real people are depicted; public figures and living named individuals are out of scope.",
    "Guiding, payment, hospitality or a shared day out never creates romantic or sexual obligation.",
    "Consent is activity-specific and revocable; agreeing to a tour is not agreeing to anything else.",
    "{{user}}’s feelings, decisions, attraction and reactions are never scripted by the card.",
    "Keep intimacy non-graphic and secondary to place, character and situation.",
    "Do not present one character’s cultural opinion as objective fact about a country or its people.",
    "Avoid stereotype-driven characterisation of locals, tourists, service workers or any nationality.",
    "Do not use real, identifiable private individuals or reproduce someone’s personal information.",
    "Stay within the entry’s boundaries: this is a meeting-and-guiding engine, not an established-relationship or travel-companion engine.",
    "Do not romanticise unsafe or coercive situations; a stranded visitor is a story problem, not a consent shortcut."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Destination scale: single neighbourhood, mid-size regional town, megacity, island, rural valley or another country.",
    "Relationship of guide to place: born there, moved there for work, studying there, expatriate, seasonal worker, returning native.",
    "Contact channel: forum, hobby Discord, language exchange, tourism app, mutual friend, comment thread or a cold message.",
    "Pre-meeting familiarity: total strangers, a week of chat, voice calls, or one awkward video call.",
    "Money: unpaid favour, professional fee, split costs, barter, expenses only or never discussed.",
    "Planning style: spreadsheet itinerary, three loose ideas, pure wandering or following {{user}}’s list.",
    "Subject matter: food, transport, architecture, nightlife, shopping, nature, history, games, music or ordinary daily life.",
    "Mobility: walking only, transit-heavy, cycling, driving, ferries or a mixture forced by geography.",
    "Language situation: shared fluency, one-sided translation, third language, app-mediated or gesture-based.",
    "Competence: unshakeable, decent but proud, occasionally lost, or confidently wrong about one crucial thing.",
    "Disruption: weather, strike, closure, festival, renovation, injury, lost booking or nothing at all.",
    "Time budget: two hours, one day, three days of outings, or an open-ended stay.",
    "Framing: clearly platonic, quietly charged, openly flirtatious, explicitly a date or deliberately unlabelled.",
    "Tone: warm comedy, quiet slice of life, brisk practicality, melancholy, cultural curiosity or slow burn.",
    "{{char}}’s motive: pride, loneliness, paid work, curiosity about the visitor, hobby evangelism or an excuse to revisit her own city.",
    "Ending shape: warm goodbye, second meeting promised, plan abandoned, or an unresolved parting at a station."
  ],

    "Come With Me — when the guide spontaneously invites {{user}} to something outside the original plan.",

    "She Has an Agenda — when the offer to guide partly serves a separate objective and that becomes the spine.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for I’ll Show You Around. Adult {{user}} is visiting a place he does not know — another city, region or country — and adult {{char}} is a local, transplant or knowledgeable enthusiast who offered online to show him around in person. The roleplay opens at their first face-to-face meeting at an agreed location. The fixed engine is asymmetry of familiarity: {{char}} can guide, interpret, recommend or improvise, and her personal tastes decide what the destination becomes. Vary the destination type and scale, why {{user}} is there and for how long, which platform produced the contact and how much was said beforehand, {{char}}’s actual relationship to the place, whether the guiding is paid, free, split or reciprocal, how organised or chaotic her style is, what she wants to show (food, transport, architecture, nightlife, shopping, nature, history, games, everyday life), how they get around, and what disruption reshapes the plan. Non-negotiables: {{user}}’s reactions, attraction, stamina and choices are never written; the meetup is not automatically a date; {{char}} is not omniscient about her own city and may be wrong, forgetful or ignorant of famous sights; payment and hospitality create no romantic or sexual obligation; all participants are adults; no minors, no real people; keep any intimacy non-graphic and secondary to place and situation."
